subject: Weighted latency commitment & short-term pilot request for FinScale
messages:
From: Tara Nguyen <tara@finscale.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:24:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify p95 measurement across mixed payloads

Jonas — thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is evaluating Redwood for our real-time inference layer, but we have a follow-up ask around SLO measurement.

Problem: our traffic mixes short low-token requests (user chat) and periodic long-batch enrichment calls (hundreds of tokens). When your SLOs report p95 across all requests, the tail is dominated by those big enrichment jobs and our product team is uncomfortable with the impact on the commercial p95 commitment.

Request: can Redwood provide an amendment that (a) separates p50/p95 targets by request payload-size buckets, or (b) applies a token-weighted percentile so long requests don't disproportionately move the commercial p95? We need something that is auditable for procurement and our compliance folks.

We'd like to get alignment this month — can your team propose a concrete wording and recommended measurement window? Also flagging: we expect a 10-day migration where enrichment jobs run at ramped volume; would appreciate a short-term carveout during that window if needed.

Thanks,
Tara Nguyen
Head of Platform, FinScale

--
FinScale | tara@finscale.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara@finscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify p95 measurement across mixed payloads

Tara — really helpful context, thanks. Attached is a concise proposal that addresses both asks. High-level summary here so you can share with procurement quickly: 

1) Split percentile commitments by token buckets: small (<=64 tokens) and large (>64 tokens). Commercial commitments will be: p50 <= 60ms and p95 <= 180ms for small bucket; p50 <= 120ms and p95 <= 800ms for large bucket.

2) Token-weighted percentile alternative: we can measure a weighted p95 where each request contributes proportionally to token count; recommendation: only offered when both parties agree during contract negotiation — it is more computationally involved for auditing.

3) Measurement horizon: 30-day rolling window for contractual reporting, with a 7-day operational window used for alerting and incident response.

4) Temporary migration carveout: 10-day grace window where we exclude scheduled enrichment maintenance runs defined in advance (max two scheduled windows in a 90-day period).

I've attached a redline-ready amendment you can review (Redwood_hosted_sla_amendment_draft.pdf). If that looks good, we'll run a short 30-day pilot (no commercial penalty) to validate metrics and sampling, then ship the amendment via DocuSign.

Would love to hop on a 30-min sync if you want to walk through specific wording.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 206-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_hosted_sla_amendment_draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

From: Tara Nguyen <tara@finscale.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify p95 measurement across mixed payloads

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround. The split buckets approach looks reasonable to our product and procurement teams; the numbers you proposed are close to what our internal SLA team expects. A couple of asks before we move to DocuSign: 

- Can you add an explicit audit log clause: Redwood will provide raw percentile computation logs (anonymized request ids, timestamps, token counts, latency sample) for any disputed month within 60 days?
- Can the 30-day pilot be executed starting Nov 20 so we can sync with our deployment window?

If you can add that audit clause and start the pilot Nov 20, we'll be prepared to approve the amendment pending legal review.

Best,
Tara

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Clarify p95 measurement across mixed payloads — pricing & ops impact

Team — forwarding Tara's confirmation and the two asks (audit logs + Nov 20 pilot start). Please review the attached Ops impact workbook and comment inline. Quick notes: 

- Ops impact: estimating ~0.6% infra uplift to enable request-level token tagging and persist sampling logs for 60 days; engineering prefers the token-bucket split for simplicity. See slo-amendment-ops-impact.xlsx.
- Pricing: if we accept the split buckets at the suggested numbers, we may need a modest uplift on the committed throughput tier for FinScale — recommend +10% on committed capacity for the first quarter of the pilot to avoid tail saturation.
- Legal: Marissa, can you fast-track a redline that includes a narrow audit-log clause (anonymized, read-only export, 60-day window)?

I plan to send Tara a revised amendment with the audit clause + pilot dates once we align. Thoughts?

—Jonas

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify p95 measurement across mixed payloads — pricing & ops impact

LGTM. A couple of practical edits to the amendment: 

- Make the token thresholds configurable by mutual agreement (default 64 tokens) and include an appendix with sample traffic buckets for reproducibility.
- For the audit export, restrict fields to timestamp, token_count, anonymized_request_hash, latency_ms, and measurement_bucket. No payload or PII. Export via secure S3 link with 7-day access windows.
- Confirm that the 30-day rolling reporting window is used for billing and SLO compliance; keep 7-day for alerts only.

If legal signs off on the narrow audit clause, I'm fine with the +10% committed throughput recommendation for the pilot.

Ben

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara@finscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final amendment & DocuSign link — FinScale pilot start Nov 20

Tara — thanks for the quick review and clarity. We made the edits Ben suggested and Marissa's team approved the narrow audit language. Summary of final changes: 

• Token buckets remain the default split with configurable threshold (default 64 tokens).
• Audit export: anonymized_request_hash, timestamp, token_count, latency_ms, measurement_bucket. Secure S3 export, 60-day retention, one-click 7-day download link for audited months.
• Measurement windows: 30-day rolling for contractual reporting, 7-day operational for alerting.
• Migration carveout: 10-day scheduled exclusion windows as proposed.
• Pilot: starts Nov 20, 2026; Redwood will provision +10% committed throughput for the pilot period. No commercial penalties for pilot anomalies.

I've uploaded the final redline and created a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://docusign.net/Sign?doc=FS-2026-021

Please sign the DocuSign by Nov 19 so we can start the pilot on Nov 20. If you'd like a 30-minute run-through of the final wording, I can schedule for Nov 18.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 206-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_hosted_sla_amendment_draft.pdf, slo-amendment-ops-impact.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)
